questionText:
Read the following consumer rights case study and answer the questions that follow:

Sunita purchased an electric water geyser from a local home appliance store for Rs. 12,500. She paid the full amount in cash and received a printed cash memo. Within two weeks of installation, the geyser malfunctioned due to defective heating element insulation, giving her a severe electric shock. Upon examining the appliance closely, Sunita noticed that the geyser did not bear the mandatory ISI standardisation mark from the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS). When she approached the retail store owner demanding a replacement or full refund, the retailer flatly refused, pointing to a handwritten note on the receipt stating 'Goods once sold will not be taken back or exchanged'. Sunita consulted a Voluntary Consumer Organization (VCO) and filed an online consumer complaint on the e-Daakhil portal under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, claiming refund and compensation under Product Liability for mental agony and injury.

Question: Why is the ISI mark from the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) legally mandatory on domestic electric water geysers?

options.text: It guarantees that the appliance complies with national safety standards to protect users against electric shocks and fire hazards.

options.text: It certifies that the appliance meets eco-friendly energy efficiency standards to reduce power consumption.
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: It verifies that the appliance is imported and compliant with international trade pricing regulations.
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: It serves as an aesthetic quality seal issued by voluntary trade associations for premium appliances.
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
For Mandatory Certification Mark on Geysers (Resource Management):
Electric water heaters involve risks of electrocution and fire hazards. Mandatory ISI certification from the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) guarantees that the appliance adheres to national safety standards to prevent electrical shocks and operational hazards.

Therefore, option (A) is the correct answer.
